Caption: 

“When we reach the point when the world produces all the goods that it needs in two days, as it inevitably will, we must curtail our production of goods and turn our attention to the great problem of what to do with our new leisure.”
_— Julian Huxley, 1930 _



----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fecd0a16-f331-43db-bf6f-bcb11bf46198/til-apple-was-named-apple-because-steve-jobs-was-on-a-only-v0-hExbBc7Sp0jWWHeXg9ZJJd90hDRb03Ds-neTpFPJ06M.webp?t=1788554487)
Caption: 

# When jobs become hobbies

Blacksmithing has always been a loud, hot, strenuous, and dangerous activity.

Today, it’s also an expensive one.

Where bashing metal used to be a profession, people now pay for the privilege of doing it. $325 for an [intro to blacksmithing](https://www.brandrforge.net/bf-blades-1-1) class in Brooklyn, NY, for example. Or $925 for a three-day “[adult summer camp](https://www.nazzforge.com/adult-camp-2026-copy).” 

Blacksmithing hasn’t really been a profession since about 1930, by which time, pretty much everything traditionally made by hand — nails, tools, samurai swords — was being made in factories. 

Horseshoes were the last holdout of commercial blacksmithing because they were so bespoke (every horse hoof is different). When horses were replaced by automobiles, blacksmiths lost that work, too.

At that point, a blacksmith’s best chance for continued employment was perhaps[ Colonial Williamsburg](https://www.colonialwilliamsburg.org/events/blacksmith/), where they plied their trade in front of an audience — demonstrating how metal products were made in the days before factories made everything.

It’s still a popular attraction, and not just for the blacksmiths. Colonial Williamsburg also has weaving, brickmaking, cordwaining (leather shoes), basketmaking, wheelwrighting (wagon wheels), coopering (barrels), and book binding — all the lost professions of the 19th century, performed for history-buff tourists.   

Being something of a history-buff tourist myself, I can’t help wondering: How long will it be before people want to watch programmers work, too? 

Because writing code — line by line — is quickly becoming as antiquated as binding your own books.

Soon, crafting functions, loops, and if-then statements will be a lost art, practiced only by a small group of artisanal programmers.

78714.subject: 🔷 The Daily: 'White-hat' hackers return most of the $320M they took from Liquid
78714.body:
South Korea's Hanwha develops tokenized securities platform on Avalanche as local regulation takes shape | Spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in $987 million last week as institutional demand recovers | Harmony to fully sunset Layer 1, proposes token migration to Ethereum for AI video initiative | LeBron James teases Polymarket partnership in new social media video |

The Daily ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by James Hunt

Presented By:

( https://bron.org/?utm_source=TheBlock&utm_medium=Email&utm_campaign=DailyNewsletter&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Happy Monday! *Bitcoin* is still trading near $80,000 despite renewed *Fed* rate hike fears, with this week's U.S. inflation data set to provide the next major test.

In today's newsletter, *Liquid Network* pauses after a 4,000 BTC purported "white-hat" incident, *Hanwha* develops a tokenized securities platform on *Avalanche* , *bitcoin ETFs* attract nearly $1 billion in weekly inflows, and more.

Meanwhile, *Hunter Biden* teased a " *LAPTOP* " project for Sept. 9, appearing to confirm a Wall Street Journal report that he plans to launch a memecoin on *Base* this week.

*P.S.* Don't forget to check out today's reader poll on *CPI* later in the newsletter.

*THE BIG ONE*

*⚠️ Liquid Network pauses after purported 'white-hat' hackers withdraw $320 million in bitcoin*

( https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2026-09-06-liquid-network-pauses-after-purported-white-hat-hackers-withdraw-320-million-in-bitcoin-413626?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*Liquid Network* paused its *Bitcoin* sidechain after purported white-hat hackers withdrew roughly 4,000 BTC, worth about $320 million, from its federation wallet.

* The withdrawal drained around 95% of Liquid's reported bitcoin reserves, which stood at about 4,200 BTC before the incident.
* An onchain message tied to the transaction read "we are whitehats. contact us onchain," with the attacker later offering to return most of the funds once the underlying bug was fixed.
* The attacker told *Blockstream* , Liquid's technology provider, to "fix the bug first" and patch every node before they would send the bitcoin back.
* Blockstream replied that its bridge nodes were patched and it was "safe to return the funds," after which the attacker returned 3,400 BTC (about 85%), keeping roughly 598.5 BTC ($47.3 million).
* *SideSwap* said the issue stemmed from a bug in the *Elements* software that minted LBTC, stressing that neither its systems nor its peg-out authorization key was compromised.
